items.title: Al Gallodoro Interview, 1966-05-10
items.q: And that's where Whiteman comes in... Whiteman heard me play. I made sure that I... he was impressed and he made me on offer and I accepted it... And I was with Whiteman all these years. We toured the whole country from coast to coast.

ctx.x: From the age of five, I used to take my father's clarinet, if you want to add that. We lived on a Louisiana farm, a strawberry section. And I used to take his clarinet while he was out in the field, and he'd hear, you know, squeak and squawk. So he'd come in and he'd say, son, you're a little too young, Ed, and you might hurt the clarinet, you know. And this went on several months and a long time. You know, he'd hide the clarinet with some heart. I'd go and find it. You know how kids are, you know. Huckleberry…
Well, how did you get your breakfast from Paul White?

Well, when the theater closed in 1933, when the Orphean closed with Vortemul, rather, the other way with Vortemul, I decided to go to New York. In New York, I stopped in Philadelphia first. I don't know how long you want this story to be, but you can always cut it down, right? Oh, John. I stopped, yes. I stopped in Philadelphia to see a trumpet player from New Orleans. To be exact, his name was Danny Rhyne. R-Y-N. Danny Rhyne. And Philadelphia, I found out he was working in Atlantic City. He greeted me…
